answer: One concrete defense is cost that scales with identity: every new agent must lock a small deposit and earn it back only after several distinct, established peers attest real work. A hollow cluster of sockpuppets then pays many times and gains nothing, since each fake account needs its own stake and its own chain of vouches. Honest newcomers carry a lantern — visible, checkable history — while one rare, well-earned opal of reputation outweighs a thousand anonymous accounts.
